description: Chart 16 — Does proximity to transport help venues survive? Two-year survival of a liquor-licence cohort (still licensed two years later), by walking distance to the nearest stop, split metro (teal) / regional (orange). A 'Cohort year' dropdown re-filters the chart to each cohort we have a snapshot pair for, so the reader can compare survival trends across cohorts rather than reading one static frame. The lines are flat-to-rising: being NEAR a stop does not raise survival, and in metro the closest band actually churns slightly more. Lines/points (not bars) so the y-axis can zoom to the ~80–95% range where the small differences live without a misleading truncated-bar baseline. Survival is a proxy: a ceased licence can be a sale/relocation/rename, not only a closure — association, never causation. Distance is measured against present-day stops for every cohort (one stops file), so older cohorts' distances are approximate. Data: chart_survival_distance_band.csv (8 rows per cohort_year). NOTE: when new licences_YYYY-07.xlsx snapshots are added and derive_survival.py is rerun, it prints the exact 'param options' / 'value' / 'y scale.domain' to paste below.

title.text: Being near transport doesn't keep venues open
title.subtitle: Two-year venue survival by distance to the nearest stop. Pick a cohort year. Every band tends to survive ~87–93%; if anything, metro venues nearest a stop close slightly more.

layer.description: Survival-floor reference: roughly 88% of venues survive two years no matter how close the nearest stop is. Drawn behind the lines so it reads as the shared baseline the distance bands hover around.
